heroHeadline: New Front Opens at Mwenga's Point Zéro as FARDC Accuses AFC/M23-RDF of Fresh Walikale-Masisi Attacks; Ebola Deaths Pass 3,639 as Outbreak Reaches Seventh Province
heroSubtitle: Clashes intensified from the morning of Sept 19 at Point Zéro in South Kivu's Mwenga territory, pitting a FARDC-Wazalendo coalition backed by Burundian forces against an AFC/Red Tabara-Twirwaneho coalition, with fighting spreading into Fizi's Natulonge, Kabindo, Biziba and Irumba villages and displacing residents across the Fizi-Uvira-Itombwe highlands. On Sept 20, FARDC's Sokola 1 Grand-Nord sector accused AFC/M23-RDF forces of fresh attacks on the Walikale-Masisi axis, burning villages and destroying crops and driving new displacement toward Walikale — this after a FARDC communiqué on Sept 17 claimed 14 AFC/M23 fighters killed across Walikale, Masisi and Rutshuru since Sept 15, and a day after Beni police and FARDC arrested 28 people, including two soldiers, in a Sept 19 sweep of the Malepe neighborhood following the Sept 10 Butanuka triple killing. DRC's Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak reached 7,541 confirmed cases and 3,639 deaths per INSP's Sept 18 data (48.3% case-fatality rate), spreading to a seventh province, Sud-Ubangi, via an imported case; the response marked a milestone Sept 19 as the first participants were vaccinated in Bunia under a 20,000-person Ervebo clinical trial testing efficacy against the Bundibugyo strain, which currently has no approved vaccine.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
